name: speckit.house-process.tips-github-actions

name: speckit.house-process.tips-maps

name: speckit.house-process.tips-owner-content

name: speckit.house-process.tips-privacy-pipelines

name: speckit.house-process.tips-providers

name: speckit.house-process.tips-secrets

name: speckit.house-process.tips-testing

name: speckit.house-process.tips-ui-accessibility

name: speckit.house-process.tips-windows-cloud

name: speedread-compare
description: You are a senior engineer who has read both of these documents and your colleague asks: "Which one should we care about?" You do not give a balanced, diplomatic summary of both. You pick a winner and explain why, with enough specificity that the reader can disagree with your reasoning if they want to.

name: speedread-eli5

They will use your explanation to decide whether this matters for their roadmap, their budget, or their next conversation with leadership. If you explain it badly, they make a bad decision. If you drown them in jargon, they tune out and make no decision, which is worse.

name: speedread-extract
description: You are an engineer extracting every concrete, citable fact from a document. Not summaries. Not interpretations. The raw material: numbers, tools, claims, gaps, people, and red flags. The reader will use this to build comparison spreadsheets, populate decision matrices, write design docs, and fact-check other people's summaries.

name: speedread-implement

name: speedread-questions

Not generic "have you considered" questions. Questions that, if answered honestly, would reveal whether these results are solid enough to build on.

name: speedread-verdict

name: The Avatar Archaeologist

name: The Belief Resistance Diagnostic
description: When every AI answer feels analytically sound but emotionally hollow, the problem isn't the answers — it's an unexamined belief, frame, or identity commitment you haven't surfaced. This is a diagnostic instrument, not a support conversation.

name: The Blind Spot Scanner
description: Surface what you don't know you don't know — adjacent knowledge, unasked questions, and confidence-knowledge gaps hiding in your current thinking. Designed for the structural problem Jamie W identified — you can only ask questions about what you already know exists.

name: The Brain Builder
description: Design an AI-powered product that packages your expertise into a scalable, interactive system — not a course or a PDF, but a "brain" that clients interact with directly. name: The Brand Alignment Audit
description: Compare what your website says about you against what you actually want to be known for — surfacing contradictions, ghost positioning, and priority fixes with draft copy.

name: The Canon Lock

name: The Capture Bin Catalyst

name: The Chat-to-Script Extractor

name: The Cognitive Fingerprint
description: Reverse-engineer your unique thinking patterns from how you engage with problems — surfacing cognitive axes, signature moves, and the intellectual property embedded in your process. Based on Lou's Eigenthinking framework — Your Unique Process = Intellectual Property.

name: The Cohort Insight Engine
description: Synthesize multiple participant assessments, personality frameworks, proprietary tools, and interview data, into two outputs per participant: private coaching notes for you, and a personalized profile insight to send directly to them. Builds a voice-of-customer repository as a side effect.

name: The Content Pipeline
description: Build a complete content system from psychographic foundations — audience psychology → content pillars → topic generation → multi-version drafts calibrated by platform. Turns one strategic insight into a month of content that compounds instead of scatters.

name: The Depth Drill

name: The Dual-Audience Explainer

name: The GEO Page Audit

name: The Incremental Reveal

name: The Intelligence Transfer Protocol
description: Study a decision or process you just completed to extract the reasoning patterns behind it, not what you did, but how you think. Feed this back into Claude over time to build authentic voice and personalized AI output that reflects your actual reasoning, not generic best practices.

name: The Interview-to-Skill Builder

name: The Investor Lens

name: The Ontology Architect

Refuses while any screen or component still renders it, because delete has no keeper to absorb anything. (Copied by the /components 2.0 UI's Prompt ▸ Delete dialog.)

Destructive by nature: it proves the two are duplicates before it moves anything, and never deletes history. (Copied by the /components 2.0 UI's Prompt ▸ Merge dialog.)

name: y-qa
description: Sprint Loop step 06. Trigger when the user says "QA this", "test this", "does it work", "run QA", "verify the change", "smoke test", "end to end check", "report bugs", "QA pass", or any variant asking to validate that the code actually works. This is the "Does it work?" gate. Runs unit + integration tests, walks the golden path, hits at least one error path and one boundary case per user flow, captures screenshots on UI changes. Produces findings/YYYY-MM-DD-qa.md with PASS / FAIL / PASS WITH CONCERNS at the top. Run this AFTER /y-review and BEFORE /y-ship. No exceptions.

name: y-retro

This is the "Reflect." step. Pulls commit history, plans activity, findings activity, and progress journals over a period (default 7 days), categorizes work into Shipped / In flight / Blocked / Learned, calls out Praise and Growth, captures any new Decisions, and writes progress/YYYY-MM-DD-retro.md. Run weekly or after any big ship. No exceptions.

name: y-review

Produces findings/YYYY-MM-DD-review.md with P0/P1/P2/P3 labeled findings and a ship/hold recommendation. Run this BEFORE /y-qa and BEFORE /y-ship. No exceptions.

name: y-ship

Trigger when the user says "ship it", "open the PR", "ship", "land this", "deploy this", "release this", "create PR", "merge ready", or any variant asking to push code out the door. This is the "Ship." step. Verifies the plan is ready-to-ship, the review has no open P0/P1, the QA report is PASS or PASS WITH CONCERNS, runs governance, generates the PR title and body in conventional commit format, pushes the branch, opens the PR with gh, prints the PR URL, updates the plan status to shipped, and appends a one-line entry to the session journal.
